algorithm: Gaussian Naive Bayes with log-space scoring

classes.desc: Naive Bayes classifier with Gaussian feature likelihoods.
classes.name: GaussianNB

complexity: O(n*d) to fit n samples with d features; O(c*d) per prediction
data_flow_ascii:
--seed -> generate_dataset -> split_dataset (train/test)
train -> GaussianNB.fit (priors + per-feature mean/var)
test -> GaussianNB.predict -> accuracy + confusion matrix
description_sentence: Trains a Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier on seeded synthetic features and reports priors, accuracy, and the confusion matrix.
failure_note: A tiny epsilon is added to every variance so a constant feature cannot cause division by zero; ties in log-scores break toward the lower class label deterministically.

functions.desc: Generate 2-feature topic vectors with binary labels.
functions.name: generate_dataset

functions.desc: Shuffle and split into (X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test).
functions.name: split_dataset

functions.desc: Estimate per-class priors and per-feature (mean, var).
functions.name: GaussianNB.fit

functions.desc: Return the most likely class for each feature vector.
functions.name: GaussianNB.predict

functions.desc: Parse args, train, and print accuracy and confusion matrix.
functions.name: main

label: Naive Bayes classifier
output_shape: Train/test sizes, class priors, test accuracy, and a confusion matrix (rows=true, cols=predicted).
pitch_sentence: A {topic} Naive Bayes classifier in pure Python that learns Gaussian feature likelihoods from seeded data and proves itself with a confusion matrix.

qa.a: Yes; scores are accumulated in log space, which avoids underflow when multiplying many small probabilities.
The demo uses two Gaussian blobs per class in two dimensions, but the classifier itself works for any feature count.
qa.q: What features does the demo use?

qa.a: --train-frac controls the split; the default 0.7 keeps 30 percent of samples for testing.
qa.q: How is the test set made?

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} Naive Bayes classifier in pure Python with Gaussian likelihoods and log-space scoring; demo trains on seeded synthetic data and reports accuracy with a confusion matrix.
scaling_note: Pure-Python loops over features make this fine for thousands of samples; larger or high-dimensional data would want vectorization.
storage_note: In-memory only: the dataset and learned priors/parameters exist for the run and are not persisted.
tradeoff_note: Naive Bayes assumes feature independence, which is fast and simple but can underperform correlated-feature models on real data.
